2026-12-27.title: First Sunday after Yaldo
readings: The return from Egypt to Nazareth
The boy Samson grows and the Lord blesses him
Let us go to the house of the Lord
Old and young in the streets of Jerusalem
Christ, faithful as a Son over God's house
The boy Jesus in the Temple
2026-12-27.alt: Season of Yaldo–Denho. Today is also the Commemoration of the Infants killed by Herod (27 December, as in the 2025–26 lectionary).
2026-12-27.verse: Then he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was obedient to them. His mother treasured all these things in her heart.
theo: Two days after Yaldo the Church turns to the hidden life of the Holy Family. Matthew tells how Joseph, warned in a dream, brought the Child and his mother back from Egypt and “made his home in a town called Nazareth”. Luke shows the family going up each year to Jerusalem for the Passover. The Son of God grows up in an ordinary family, in an ordinary village, keeping the ordinary feasts of his people.

At twelve, Jesus stays behind in the Temple. After three days of anxious searching his parents find him “sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions.” Mary says, “Your father and I have been searching for you in great anxiety.” Jesus answers: “Why were you searching for me? Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house?” His first recorded words reveal who his true Father is.

And yet, the Gospel says, “he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was obedient to them.” The eternal Son obeys a carpenter and a village woman. Hebrews says Christ is “faithful over God's house as a son, and we are his house”. The family of Nazareth is the school where the Son of God learned to be human: to work, to pray, to obey and to grow “in wisdom and in years, and in divine and human favor”.

Zechariah's vision of Jerusalem is a picture of a blessed family and city: “Old men and old women shall again sit in the streets… and the streets of the city shall be full of boys and girls playing.” Families where the old are honoured and children are safe and joyful are signs of God's kingdom. Today we also remember the infants killed by Herod: the Church has always honoured them as martyrs, and with them we pray for every threatened child.
conn: Like Israel, and like Joseph son of Jacob, the Child goes down to Egypt and comes up again (Hosea 11:1; Matthew 2:15). He relives his people's story to save it.
Samson grew “and the LORD blessed him” (Judges 13:24); Isaac grew and was weaned (Genesis 21:8); Jesus “increased in wisdom and in years” (Luke 2:52).
Going up to the house of the Lord.
Psalm 122, “I was glad when they said to me, Let us go to the house of the LORD”, was a pilgrim song. The Holy Family sang such psalms on the road to Jerusalem.
Twice Luke says Mary kept these things in her heart (2:19, 51). She is the first contemplative of the Gospel.
altar: The boy Jesus said he must be in his Father's house. Every Sunday we too are called to our Father's house, the church, to listen and to receive. Families who come to Holy Qurbono together are walking the road of Nazareth to Jerusalem.
outline: Ask parents: have you ever lost a child for a few minutes in a crowd? Recall that fear.
Point 1 · God in an ordinary family
Nazareth: work, prayer, obedience, feasts. Holiness is possible at home.
Jesus' first words: his identity and mission. Teach children that the church is their Father's house.
The Son of God obeyed. Children obey, parents listen, all grow.
Pray for every threatened child: the unborn, the abused, children of war.
live: Choose one fixed time for family prayer every day this week, even ten minutes.
Bring children to the Father's house
Come to Holy Qurbono as a family, sitting together, and talk about the Gospel on the way home.
Visit or call grandparents and older relatives during this Christmas season.
fathers: He notes that Jesus, at twelve, shows his divinity in the Temple and his humanity in submitting to his parents: the One who is Lord of all becomes subject out of love (Exposition of the Gospel of Luke 2).
He sings of the Child of Nazareth who grew in the house of Joseph, the Son of the Most High obeying a carpenter, and of Mary who was mother and disciple at once (Hymns on the Nativity).
magis: The hidden life at Nazareth: Jesus shares the condition of the vast majority of people, a daily life of manual work, obedience and prayer; the finding in the Temple reveals his total consecration to the Father.
The Holy Family of Nazareth is a model and a light for every family; the covenant of love is lived in daily life.
The Christian family as the domestic Church.
saints: 27 Dec: Commemoration of the Infants killed by Herod. 1 Jan: Naming of our Lord; New Year. 2 Jan: Mar Baselios and Mar Gregory, name day of our Major Archbishop-Catholicos Moran Mor Baselios Cardinal Cleemis. 3 Jan: St Kuriakose Elias Chavara. Confirm in the 2026–27 lectionary.
2026-12-27.prayer: Lord Jesus, you grew up in the home of Mary and Joseph at Nazareth, obedient to them and busy with your Father's affairs. Bless our families: make our homes places of prayer, work and love, protect every child, and honour every elder. Amen.

quick: The Son of God grew up in an ordinary family at Nazareth.
“I must be in my Father's house”: Jesus' first words.
He went down to Nazareth and was obedient: holiness at home.
2026-12-27.action: Set a fixed time for family prayer every day this week.
2026-12-27.question: Is my home a little Nazareth?
2026-12-27.special: First Sunday after Yaldo. Commemoration of the Infants killed by Herod.
illus: A Kerala father once lost his small son at a crowded church festival. For an hour he ran from stall to stall. When he found the boy sitting calmly near the altar, he did not know whether to scold him or hold him. Mary and Joseph knew that feeling.

family.explain: When Jesus was twelve, he stayed behind in the Temple, and his parents searched for him for three days. Jesus said the Temple was his Father's house. Then he went home with them and obeyed them.
family.intention: We pray for our family, that we may love, obey and help one another like the Holy Family.
family.ask: Ask: “How can each of us make our home more like Nazareth this week?”

catechism: The Christian family, a communion of persons.
kidsaint: Jesus, Mary and Joseph lived in a small house. Joseph worked as a carpenter, Mary cared for the home, and Jesus helped and obeyed them. They prayed together and went to the Temple. Lesson: your family can be holy too.
term: The small village in Galilee where Jesus grew up and lived about thirty years. Christians were first nicknamed “Nazarenes” (Acts 24:5); in Kerala the old name “Nasrani” for St Thomas Christians comes from the same word.
termMore: The children of Bethlehem killed by Herod (Matthew 2:16–18). The Church honours them as the first martyrs for Christ, who died not speaking but in his place.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you lived in Nazareth with Mary and Joseph after the return from Egypt. As we gather on the First Sunday after Yaldo, bless our families. Amen.
share: The Holy Family settled in Nazareth after exile (Matthew 2:19–23). What journeys has my family made?
Peter says: clothe yourselves with humility (1 Peter 5:5). Where is humility needed in my home?
What would make our home more like Nazareth?
pm.resp: Jesus, Mary and Joseph, bless our family.
interc: For all families, that they may imitate the Holy Family.
For families separated by work abroad.
For broken families, that they may be healed.
pm.close: Lord God, you gave your Son a home in Nazareth. Bless our families with faith, humility and love, and keep us united in you. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, two days after Yaldo, the Church takes us into the house at Nazareth. The Son of God did not grow up in a palace. He lived in a small village, in a carpenter's home, with Mary and Joseph, keeping the feasts of his people.

Every year they went up to Jerusalem for the Passover. When Jesus was twelve, he stayed behind in the Temple. Parents here know the fear Mary and Joseph felt: three days of searching! When they found him, Jesus said: “Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house?” These are his first words in the Gospel. He knew who his true Father was.

And yet the next verse says: “he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was obedient to them.” The Lord of heaven obeyed a carpenter and a village mother. For about thirty years he lived a hidden life of work, prayer and obedience. Holiness does not begin in great deeds; it begins at home.

Today we also remember the little children killed by Herod. Let us pray for every child in danger: the unborn, children who suffer violence, children of war and hunger. And let us make our homes little Nazareths: with daily family prayer, respect for elders, and joy for children. Amen.
kids: Children, when Jesus was twelve, he went with Mary and Joseph to the big Temple in Jerusalem. On the way home, they couldn't find him! They searched for three days.
They found Jesus in the Temple, listening and asking questions. He said: “This is my Father's house!” Then he went home and obeyed Mary and Joseph.
Jesus obeyed his parents. Can you do that too? Let's say: “Like Jesus, I will love and obey!”

intro: Theme: “The Holy Family: a home where God grows.”
After Christmas the Church looks at the home where Jesus grew up. The Son of God chose to live thirty years in an ordinary family at Nazareth. Our families can become holy in the same ordinary ways.

points.h: A family that goes to God's house together
sub: Every year Mary and Joseph went up to Jerusalem for the Passover.
At twelve, Jesus stays in the Temple: “I must be in my Father's house.”
Parents first teach children to love God's house by going there gladly themselves.
q: I was glad when they said to me, “Let us go to the house of the LORD!”
He said to them, “Why were you searching for me? Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house?”
points.apply: Come to the Holy Qurbono as a whole family, on time, every Sunday.

sub: Jesus returns to Nazareth and is obedient to Mary and Joseph.
Proverbs teaches children to listen to a father's instruction and a mother's teaching.
Mary treasures everything in her heart: family life needs reflection and prayer, not only work.
q: Hear, my child, your father's instruction, and do not reject your mother's teaching.

Then he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was obedient to them. His mother treasured all these things in her heart. And Jesus increased in wisdom and in years, and in divine and human favor.
points.apply: Children: obey your parents with a cheerful heart this week. Parents: spend unhurried time with your children.

points.h: A family protected by God through trials
sub: The Holy Family knew danger, exile and fear.
Joseph rises at God's word and brings them safely home.
God promises to dwell among his people “in faithfulness and in righteousness”.
q: I will bring them to live in Jerusalem. They shall be my people and I will be their God, in faithfulness and in righteousness.
Get up, take the child and his mother, and go to the land of Israel, for those who were seeking the child's life are dead.
points.apply: Pray together for families in crisis: separated, sick, in debt or abroad.

concl: Nazareth teaches us silence, work and love. Holiness grows at the family table, in prayer together and in daily obedience.
May Jesus, Mary and Joseph make our homes little Nazareths.
2026-12-27.resolve: Begin or renew evening family prayer, and consecrate your family to the Holy Family.
